With CEO, with correctness and efficiency only, the idea of getting close doesn't even come up. If the whole idea of correctness and efficiency, the way it works is the later steps trust that the earlier steps

cues.en: computational model and scale it indefinitely large that we can keep on adding more and more computing power to it as long as we have money to buy the nodes and power to power them and space, real estate, to plug them all together. To do that we need to focus on robustness. This computer potentially could be so big we cannot finish it before we start using it.

The computations that we build have to be inherently robust so that we can slap this stuff together and make it work. Okay, let's see what it looks like.
cues.zh: 我们可以在系统运行的同时接入更多设备。它的规模会大到在运行过程中，总有一部分在被修复，或者以各种方式出故障。我们构建的计算系统必须天生具备强鲁棒性，这样我们才能随手把组件拼在一起并让它正常工作。好，来看看它到底长什么样。

cues.en: I don't know if this is visible or not. This is a grid here. The movable feast, this version, is a two-dimensional grid of individual sites. Each site can hold a small amount of information on the order of dozens of bits, perhaps, or hundreds maybe, but not on the order of kilobytes or megabytes.
cues.zh: 不知道大家能不能看清。这里是一个网格。Movable Feast 的这个版本，是由一个个独立位点（site）组成的二维网格。每个位点能容纳少量信息，大概几十位，或者几百位，但绝不是千字节或兆字节的数量级。

cues.en: But in addition each location each site has a certain amount of processing power so that we can have a bunch of things going on at once Okay, and in each site it can either be empty or we can have an atom one atom Here's an atom. It's called dreg stands for dynamic regulator
cues.zh: 不过此外，每个位置、每个位点都具备一定的处理能力，这样我们就能同时并行处理很多任务。好的，每个位点要么是空的，要么可以容纳一个原子——刚好一个。这里有个原子，叫 dreg，代表动态调节器（dynamic regulator）。

cues.en: Now when this guy takes his turn, when, you know, whatever, he wakes up and says, okay, compute, what he does is he looks at his neighborhood and decides what to do according to the behavior rules of dregs. So the way we program this thing is by building elements. We say elements of type dreg, when they behave, they do this. Elements of type res, when they behave, they do that, and so on. Build elements, we make them up.
cues.zh: 当轮到这家伙运行、比如它被唤醒开始计算时，它会查看周围的邻域，并根据 dreg 的行为规则来决定做什么。所以我们为这套系统编程的方式，就是构建元素。比如 dreg 类型的元素，执行时会做这个；res 类型的元素，执行时会做那个，以此类推。构建元素，也就是我们自定义它们。

cues.en: We build their behavior functions, and we come up with configurations to do some useful computation of some sort. When a drag atom runs, when any atom runs, it's not like they can access the entire grid. There is no global origin on this grid. There's no 0-0. That's why the grid fades out at the edges. From the point of view of a given atom, he is 0-0. She is 0-0.
cues.zh: 我们编写它们的行为函数，并设计配置来实现某种有用的计算。当一个 dreg 原子运行时，或者说任何原子运行时，它们都无法访问整个网格。这个网格上没有全局原点，没有所谓的 (0, 0)。这也是为什么网格边缘是渐渐隐去的。从某个特定原子的角度来看，它自己就是 (0, 0)。

cues.en: Indexing is all relative to the self. And it's very short range. This diamond shape is called the event window. That is the limits of the number of sites that this guy in the middle can access when he executes. So there's 41 sites total.
cues.zh: 所有寻址都是相对于自身的，而且范围非常小。这个菱形区域被称为事件窗口（event window）。这就是中间这家伙执行时能访问的位点范围上限。总共包含 41 个位点。

cues.en: They are all within a distance of four counting in city block distance. Four straight, one, two, three, four, one, two, three, four, make a turn, and so on. And when this guy in the center is executing, he can read and write to the event window arbitrarily. But once he gives up control at the end of his event, then some other guy gets picked, and he can read and write the event window, which might be overlapping, might be completely separate.
cues.zh: 按曼哈顿距离计算，它们都在距离 4 的范围内。比如直走四步：一、二、三、四；或者一、二、三、四再拐个弯，等等。当中心的原子执行时，它可以随意读写事件窗口。但一旦事件结束、它交出控制权，就会有另一个原子被选中，它也可以读写自己的事件窗口——这两个窗口可能会重叠，也可能完全分开。

cues.en: The movable feast machine as a whole can be executing many events simultaneously as long as none of their event windows overlap. Okay, this guy is all alone in this picture. Here's perhaps a more realistic little thing. We've got a few other atoms of some sort. Now, the way Dreg specifically works, because we're going to look at it in a second, is this. When it acts, when it behaves, it looks north, south, east, or west. One of those locations picked at random.
cues.zh: 整个 Movable Feast Machine 可以同时并发执行很多事件，只要它们的事件窗口互不重叠就行。好，在这个画面里它还是孤零零的一个。这里有个可能更贴合实际的小例子，我们放了几个其他类型的原子。Dreg 的具体工作原理是这样的（我们马上会看到）：当它行动时，它会在东、南、西、北四个方向中随机挑选一个方向看过去。

cues.en: to see whether it's empty or occupied. And, for example, suppose it looks north, it's empty. When it's empty, it picks some random number, and with some low odds, it will create a resource atom, and then I'm calling res, in that spot. And with a very low probability, instead of creating a res, it'll create another drag. Okay? So drag can reproduce into empty spots, but it's very low odds.
cues.zh: 看看它是空的还是被占用的。比如，假设它看向北边，发现是空的。如果为空，它会取一个随机数，并以较低的概率在那个位置创建一个资源原子——我称之为 res。还有极低的概率，它不会创建 res，而是创建另一个 drag。明白吧？所以 drag 可以在空位上繁殖，但概率极低。

cues.en: On the other hand, if it looks in the direction, in this case, if it looks west, it finds it's occupied, it picks a different random number with a different probability, and maybe just erases the thing. Whatever it is. Okay. And that's basically its rules. And then whatever it did at the end of the step, it diffuses. It considers moving randomly one square, north, south, east, or west. Assuming it can. Assuming it's
cues.zh: 另一方面，如果它朝某个方向看，比如往西看，发现被占用了，它就会取另一个随机数、按不同的概率，可能直接清除掉那东西，不管那是什么。行。这基本上就是它的规则。然后不管它这一步做了什么，最后都会进行扩散。它会考虑随机向东、南、西或北移动一格。前提是它能移动。前提是它……

cues.en: not all boxed in and in general diffusion respects whatever constraints there are on the local layout okay that's it that's the drag rule so can you imagine if you started with a piece of grid with one drag in it and you let it start to have events what would happen let's take a look here's a grid it's a simulator so it's a finite grid we've got one drag in it and we'll start it up
cues.zh: 没有被彻底堵死，而且通常扩散会遵循局部布局的所有约束。好了，这就是 drag 的规则。那么你能想象一下，如果从一个只有一个 drag 的网格开始，让它开始产生事件，会发生什么吗？我们来看一下，这里有一个网格，这是一个模拟器，所以是有限网格，里面有一个 drag，我们把它启动起来。

cues.en: So, there, it was just diffusing around. And eventually, it will get lucky and decide to make something. Now, it can't destroy anything because it's the only thing that there is in the universe. There, it made a res. The res does nothing. It just floats around, just diffusing the way everything does, unless it actually stops itself from diffusing. And this is all, you know, fairly boring.
cues.zh: 看，它刚才只是在周围扩散游走。最终，它会碰上运气，决定造出点东西来。现在它无法销毁任何东西，因为它是整个宇宙里唯一的存在。看，它生成了一个 res。res 什么也不做，就只是飘来飘去，像所有东西一样扩散，除非它主动停止扩散。你知道，这一切都还挺无聊的。

cues.en: But it's just warming up. Let's get rid of the grid because it gets visually a little crowded. We're artificially slowing this down so that we can get a little clue what's going on. Let's let it run at its natural speed. And you see what starts to happen. If you can read these numbers over here, there's currently 2, 1, 1. There's 50 res, 60 res, and so on.
cues.zh: 但这只是热身。我们把网格线去掉，因为视觉上看着有点挤。我们之前特意放慢了速度，好弄清楚发生了什么。现在让它按自然速度运行。大家可以看到接下来发生了什么。如果能看清这边的数字，目前是 2、1、1。有 50 个 res、60 个 res，等等。

cues.en: Overall, there's 18-19% of this little grid is occupied by something. If we let it run, given the particular probabilities I picked for creating stuff versus destroying stuff, it's basically twice as likely to erase something if it sees an occupied spot versus creating something if it sees an empty spot.
cues.zh: 总体上，这个小网格有 18% 到 19% 被占据了。如果让它继续运行，鉴于我为“创建”和“销毁”设置的特定概率，当它看到被占用的格子时清除东西的概率，基本上是它看到空格子时创建东西的两倍。

cues.en: twice as likely to destroy as to create and that tends to make it float around a third of the sites on the grid occupied. So now we're at 32%. It'll end up going a little above a third, 35%, something when it reaches equilibrium. Okay, so is this what you predicted? We get a world full of res and a few drag that are creating them and deleting them as everybody
cues.zh: 销毁概率是创建的两倍，这往往会让网格的占用率维持在三分之一左右。现在到了 32%。达到平衡时，最终会略高于三分之一，差不多 35% 左右。好了，这和你们预测的一样吗？我们得到了一个满是 res 和少量 drag 的世界，drag 负责创建和删除它们，同时所有个体

cues.en: just diffuses around. Well, so what? Well, the idea is this is a basic regulation of free space. One of the essential things about parallel computing is you have to deal with deadlock, crowding, queues full, and so on. In this robust first approach, this particular demonstration, we're saying let's just deal with that by putting in this lower level that keeps the world about one-third full.
cues.zh: 都在到处扩散。那又怎样呢？这个设计的思路是，这是一种对空闲空间的基本调控。并行计算的一个关键问题就是必须处理死锁、拥挤、队列满载等等。在这种“鲁棒优先”的方法中，在这个具体的演示里，我们的思路是：不妨通过引入这个底层机制来解决问题，让整个世界始终保持大约三分之一的充盈度。

cues.en: And if it gets much more than one third full, the dregs are going to tend to see occupied spots, so they're going to be throwing their erased shots more than their create shots, and so on. If the world gets empty, they'll see more create shots, and so on. But, we can do more with this. Suppose I put in another element. Okay, this is a guy that we'll talk about more in a second. He's a sorter, the demon horde sword. But one of the behaviors that he's got
cues.zh: 如果空间被填满超过三分之一，dreg 就会更容易看到被占用的位置，于是它们执行擦除操作的概率就会超过创建操作，以此类推。如果世界变空了，它们就会触发更多的创建操作，等等。但我们还能用它做更多事情。假设我再放进另一种元素。好，这就是我们待会儿要详细讲的家伙。它是一个 sorter，也就是 Demon Horde Sort。它具备的行为之一是……

cues.en: is he looks around himself when it's his turn to go, and if he sees res, he converts them into more sorters. Okay, so if we let this run just for a brief bit, the res have been taken over. Now if we let it run, we essentially virtually never see any res. They're still getting created by drag, but then they're getting converted into sorters essentially immediately. And this is the idea.
cues.zh: 轮到它行动时，它会环顾四周，如果看到 res，就会把它们转化成更多的 sorter。好，如果让它运行一小会儿，res 就全被接管了。现在如果让它继续跑，我们基本上就再也看不到任何 res 了。它们依然在被 dreg 创建，但几乎立刻就会被转化为 sorter。这就是核心思路。

cues.en: We can take a drag and res base and build things on top of it that will compete for the available resources and that will automatically keep their total population under control because they can only get as big as the number of resources. Okay, well let's see a little bit more about what sorters do. This is a cartoon of the world of a sorter.
cues.zh: 我们可以基于 dreg 和 res 底座来构建上层结构，让它们去争夺可用资源，而且它们会自动控制总数量，因为其规模上限取决于资源数量。好，我们再来看看 sorter 具体是怎么工作的。这是一张展示 sorter 世界的示意图。

cues.en: Okay, we've got a sorter guy in the middle, we've got the event window around him, and it's got these four areas, these little two by two things, that are just part of the sorter's world view. And what the sorter is trying to do is move data items, which are these blue atoms, and the data items for purposes of this demo just carry a number, like from zero to a million or something.
cues.zh: 好的，中间是一个 sorter，周围是它的事件窗口，里面包含这四个区域——这些 2x2 的小方块，构成了 sorter 的局部视野。sorter 要做的就是移动数据项，也就是这些蓝色原子；在本演示中，这些数据项只携带一个数字，比如从 0 到 100 万左右。

cues.en: or 0 to 100 in this picture. And what the sorter does, in addition to looking around for res to convert into more sorters, he looks to his right and up to see if there's a number that's bigger than the number he's carrying.
cues.zh: 或者像图里这样是 0 到 100。除了四处寻找 res 并转化成更多 sorter 之外，sorter 还会往右上方看，检查那里是否有比自己携带的数值更大的数字。

cues.en: Because that's a number we're going to try to sort smaller numbers up bigger numbers down So if he sees a bigger number above him He would like to move it down if he sees a smaller number below him and to the right He'd like to move it up and to the left because in all cases we're going to sort from right to left So in this case the 79 is bigger than the threshold and so he'd be interested in moving it down
cues.zh: 因为我们要把较小的数字往上排，较大的数字往下排。所以如果它看到上方有更大的数字，就会想把它往下移；如果看到右下方有更小的数字，就会想把它往左上方移，因为在所有情况下我们都是从右往左排序。所以在这种情况下，79 大于阈值，因此它想把 79 往下移。

cues.en: The 24 is smaller than the threshold he'd be interested in moving it up But the destination for moving it up is all currently occupied, but we've got an empty spot So what the sorter decides to do is take the 79 Adam Copy him down to this empty spot Erase him from where he used to be so in effect moving the 79 Right to left and moving it sort of a little quantum a little increment of sorting
cues.zh: 24 小于阈值，它本想把 24 往上移，但往上移的目标位置目前都被占满了，不过下面刚好有个空位。于是 sorter 决定把 79 这个原子复制到这个空位上，并从原位置擦除，实际上就是把 79 从右往左移动了一步，推进了一点点排序增量。

cues.en: And then as the final step, the sorter updates its threshold to be the value of the atom it just moved. So at the end of this event, the 43 will have changed to a 79, and then he will be comparing other things to 79. So that's sort of a little bit like in a bucket brigade, where you're not trying to do the entire sorting job yourself, you're just trying to make things a little better.
cues.zh: 最后一步，sorter 会把自己的阈值更新为刚刚移动的原子的值。所以在这个事件结束时，43 就变成了 79，之后它就会拿 79 去和其他元素比较。这有点像流水线接力，你不需要一个人完成全部排序，只要让局部更有序一点就行。

cues.en: And by making this spatial assumption, saying that we're going to sort from the right to the left, small is up, big is down, that allows the individual sorting element to make things better. Saying, well, okay, giving them our base assumptions about geometry, I can say with some confidence that this guy should be lower than he is. Because, why? Because he's bigger than my threshold. What does that mean? Well, my threshold was set by somebody that went through recently.
cues.zh: 通过做这个空间假设——我们要从右往左排序，小的在上、大的在下——每个排序元素就能自己把局面变得更好。也就是说，把这些基本的几何假设给它们，我就能比较有把握地说：这位应该比现在更低。为什么？因为他比我的阈值大。这意味着什么？我的阈值是最近经过的某个元素设定的。

cues.en: So this guy is bigger than someone who went through, the guy who went through immediately previously. So that's how the sorting works. Let's take a look at it. So here we've got a much bigger grid than we have last time. It doesn't look bigger because the atoms are all drawn smaller. And so on the field there are these little eggs at regular intervals. Each consists of two sorters and two dregs.
cues.zh: 所以这个元素比刚经过的那个更大，也就是紧挨着前一个经过的元素。排序就是这么工作的。我们来看一下。这里这个网格比上次大得多。它看起来没那么大，是因为原子都画得更小。场上有这些按固定间隔排布的小蛋。每个小蛋由两个分拣器和两个 dreg 组成。

cues.en: And if we look on down, there's more and there's more here in the middle. Another egg. In addition, there's this guy who's an output guy. And the idea is we're sorting right to left, so eventually the data guys will reach the left and these out guys will suck them out of the system and do whatever the rest of the computation needs with them. In our case, it's just going to score them. It's going to say, well, I know what numbers ought to be coming here, and we'll check to see how well the sorting is going.
cues.zh: 再往下看，还有更多；中间这里也更多。又一个蛋。另外，这个元素是输出元素。思路是我们从右往左排序，所以最终数据元素会到达左边，这些输出元素会把它们从系统里吸出去，交给后续计算按需处理。在我们这里，就是给它们打分。它会说：我知道这里本该出现什么数字，然后检查排序进行得怎么样。

cues.en: Similarly, over at the other end, on the right, we've got an input guy. He's going to generate data, just at random for purposes of this demo, to be sorted by the demon horde sword. And the guys in the middle are the demon horde, demon in the sense of like Maxwell's demon, you know, just making distinctions based on temperature. Here we're making them based on data. All right.
cues.zh: 同样，在另一端，也就是右边，有一个输入元素。它会生成数据——这个演示里就随机生成——交给 demon horde sword 来排序。中间这些元素就是 demon horde；这里的“妖”类似麦克斯韦妖，你知道，就是根据温度做区分。而这里我们是根据数据做区分。好。

cues.en: Now if we just had the one input guy and the one output guy, it would be everything would get incredibly clogged up around them, number one. And number two, it would be a single point of failure if something went wrong. So when I start this up in a sec, it'll be a little confusing because a bunch of stuff will be happening at once. But the first thing you'll see is the input grid will spread.
cues.zh: 如果我们只有一个输入元素和一个输出元素，第一，它们周围会堵得不可思议。第二，一旦出问题，就会变成单点故障。所以我马上启动时，会有点乱，因为一堆事情会同时发生。但你首先会看到输入网格扩散开来。

cues.en: because in addition to creating inputs, the input elements are designed to look above, look below, and if the spots where there should be another input guy don't have an input guy, and they're empty,
cues.zh: 因为输入元素除了产生输入，还会向上看、向下看；如果本该有另一个输入元素的位置没有输入元素，是空的，

cues.en: It goes ahead and puts a new input guy there. And the output grid makes a denser row of two. So we'll see the grids grow. As the input grids grow, they will start generating data, the blue atoms, and then the sorters will do their diffusion, and the drag will do their diffusion and create res, and so on. So let's take a look at its behavior. Alright, so pretty quickly...
cues.zh: 它就会在那里放一个新的输入元素。输出网格会排得更密，形成两行。所以我们会看到网格不断增长。随着输入网格增长，它们会开始生成数据，也就是蓝色原子；然后分拣器会扩散，drag 也会扩散并生成 res，等等。我们来看看它的行为。好，很快……

cues.en: We've now got a full stack of green input grid guys. They're spaced every other spot which produces the maximum amount of room in the grid for data to be added. You can still see some of the yellow guys. Those are res because the density of sorters is so low that it takes a little while before sorter notices gets into the event window of a res gets into the event window of the sorter. Now we're not doing very well.
cues.zh: 现在我们已经排满了一整列绿色的输入网格单元。它们是隔位放置的，这能让网格腾出最大空间来加入数据。你还能看到一些黄色单元。那是 Res，由于排序器密度太低，需要过一会儿 Res 才会进入排序器的事件窗口中。目前情况还不太理想。

cues.en: If we look at these things, I guess we haven't even gotten any data here. This period works in groups of 500 and we haven't gotten through one yet. But, you know, the input grid is completely clogged with data and very few have actually gotten to the output yet. But the thing, it takes a while for the machine to warm up. We've got
cues.zh: 看这边的话，我想我们甚至连数据都还没拿到。这里的周期是以 500 步为一组的，我们连一组都还没跑完。但你看，输入网格已经被数据完全堵塞了，而真正到达输出端的寥寥无几。不过这也正常，机器需要一点时间来预热。我们目前占用了

cues.en: 17% of the entire grid occupied. Once again, just because this is Dreg controlled underneath, the machine will settle in at around 35% occupied, plus or minus a bit. Alright, so now we've gotten some data.
cues.zh: 整个网格 17% 的空间。再次说明一下，因为底层是由 Dreg 控制的，机器最终的占用率会稳定在 35% 左右，上下略有浮动。好，现在我们拿到了一些数据。

cues.en: The sorting error is seven positions on average. That's pretty bad. So each of these output guys knows about, because it knows the range of numbers coming in, so it expects that it should be getting its proportionate numbers. And if it's off by, if it should be the neighboring guy, that's the sorting error of one, off by two guys, and so on. So a sorting error of, well now it's down to five, is, you know, better, still not very good.
cues.zh: 平均排序误差是 7 个位置。这相当糟糕。每个输出单元由于知晓输入数字的范围，所以它预期自己应该拿到对应区间的数字。如果偏到了相邻单元，排序误差就是 1，偏了两个单元就是 2，以此类推。所以排序误差——现在降到 5 了——虽然好一些了，但仍然不太理想。

cues.en: The categorical error is the number of data items that arrive more than eight off in either direction, sort of like, didn't even get high, medium, low, correct, sort of. And we'd like that number to be very small. But alright, let's let this run quicker and start to equilibrate a little bit. The
cues.zh: 分类误差是指在任一方向上偏差超过 8 个位置的数据项数量，差不多就像连“高中低”都没分对一样。我们希望这个数值越小越好。不过好吧，让它跑得快一点，开始逐渐达到平衡。

cues.en: overall grid occupied site density will rise. We also can focus on the delivery rate, which is the number of data items that got injected by the grid versus the number of guys that got removed by the output side during a given period of time. That number can be bigger than 100 because we might have a bunch of guys who are sort of buffered up in the grid that end up getting drained out in the next period.
cues.zh: 整个网格的占用点密度会上升。我们还可以关注投递率，也就是在给定时间段内，网格注入的数据项数量与输出端移除的数据项数量之比。这个数值可能会超过 100%，因为网格中可能缓冲了一批数据，并在下一个周期里被排空。

cues.en: But if the machine is working well, the delivery rate on average will be essentially 100%. Now we're doing a little better. The sorting errors, like down to about three and a half positions on average, plus or minus, it's not too bad. And the categorical error is a tenth of a percent, sometimes never over the course of a 500 step period. Not too bad.
cues.zh: 但如果机器运行良好，平均投递率基本就是 100%。现在情况好一些了。平均排序误差大约降到了 3.5 个位置左右，还算不错。分类误差是 0.1%，有时在 500 步的周期里甚至一次都不出现。还挺不错的。

cues.en: Now, the point of all of this is, well, it's still not equilibrating yet. So now we've got a sorter that, by its very nature, that the data comes in whenever it comes in and gets hauled through and out, that it's not even clear what correct would mean.
cues.zh: 现在这一切的关键在于——好吧，它其实还没完全达到平衡。所以我们现在的这个排序器，由于其本质特性就是数据随时进来、一路穿行然后输出，以至于连“正确”该如何定义都并不明确。

cues.en: I mean, the way the output grid is scoring it, it's relying on its knowledge of zero to a million as the possible range of numbers, and the first guy is assuming he should be getting zero to whatever, and the last guy is assuming he should be at zero, whatever it is, up to a million, and so on. But it could be the case that the input grids, because the guys are generating random numbers, might have a whole bunch of guys in a row that are all from zero to 800,000 or something, and none bigger.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，输出网格打分时，依赖的是 0 到 100 万这个预期的数值范围；排最前的以为自己该拿到 0 到某个范围的值，排最后的以为自己该拿到接近 100 万的值，诸如此类。但实际输入网格中，因为大家生成的是随机数，可能会连续出现一大批全都在 0 到 80 万之间、没有更大的数。

cues.en: And what are the sorters in the grid to do? Well, what they're going to do is they're gradually going to send those 800,000 guys all the way to the bottom because they're the biggest thing that they're seeing. And that's going to end up scoring some error from the point of view of the output grid. So the entire formulation isn't even exactly amenable to a perfectly correct solution, but it's a very natural way to judge are we getting closer or are we getting further away.
cues.zh: 那网格里的排序器会怎么做呢？它们会逐渐把这批 80 万左右的数一路送到最底下，因为这是它们见过的最大的数了。从输出网格的角度来看，这最终就会计入一些误差。所以整套设计机制甚至都不强求完全正确解，但用来衡量我们是在靠近还是远离目标，却是一种非常自然的方式。

cues.en: And this thing is embarrassingly robust. Unlike the correct first CEO approach, where you do something once, remember it, and then trust it from then on, which leaves you vulnerable if whatever you did was wrong or corrupted.
cues.zh: 而且这东西的鲁棒性强得不可思议。它不像那种“一次做对的 CEO 式做法”——做一次、记下来，从此完全信任它，一旦当初做错了或损坏了，系统就会脆弱不堪。

cues.en: Here, we are continually in the process of recreating ourselves. So if something gets screwed up, if we hit it with some x-rays, say, that just means flip random bits, like a bunch of them, like something like a third of a percent of all the bits in the machine. I don't remember exactly. If we blast it, you can see there's a bunch of hits. What happens to the sorting error as we get to the end of the next period?
cues.zh: 在这里，我们处于持续的自我重建过程中。所以如果出了问题，比如我们用 X 射线照射它——也就是随机翻转一堆 bit，比如占整台机器大约千分之三的 bit，具体记不清了。如果我们轰击它，可以看到产生了一堆命中点。等到下一个周期结束时，排序误差会发生什么变化呢？

cues.en: didn't notice. Categorical error was higher. Actually the occupied site density dropped because we can be corrupting bits that actually cause sorters to no longer be sorters, or data no longer to be data. It could be illegal types of atoms. And they just get erased. Doesn't matter. System recovers. Bleach doesn't really apply here because we don't have any bonded molecules. But Nuke, just to reset a bunch of, there we go.
cues.zh: 几乎没影响。分类误差变高了。实际上位置占用密度下降了，因为损坏的 bit 会导致排序器不再是排序器，或者数据不再是数据。可能会变成非法类型的原子，然后直接被抹掉。没关系，系统会自我恢复。Bleach 在这里不太适用，因为我们没有键合分子。但用 Nuke 重置一批……看，搞定了。

cues.en: So, just blow a hole in the corner. And what happens is, well, the output grid re-establishes itself because that's part of its normal business. And the datums, the data, all sort of collect at the leading edge of the damage because they don't have any sorters to pull them through anymore, but very quickly the sorters diffuse in from elsewhere, the drag comes back in, and the machine rebuilds itself.
cues.zh: 所以，哪怕在角落炸出一个洞，结果会怎样呢？输出网格会自行重建，因为这就是它的常规工作。而那些数据全都聚集在受损区域的边缘，因为再没有排序器来牵引它们，但很快排序器就会从其他地方扩散过来，牵引力重新恢复，机器也就完成了自我重建。

cues.en: So, and we can do something even much more radical. We can blow like two thirds of the entire machine away. And again, now the score is definitely categorical errors up to a third, sorting error is terrible. The thing is getting all jammed up here. So it takes a little longer to recover. We can look at this a variety of ways.
cues.zh: 我们甚至可以做更激进的操作，比如直接轰掉整台机器的三分之二。这时候评分肯定难看，分类误差高达三分之一，排序误差也极差，整个系统全卡在这里了。所以它需要更长一点的时间来恢复。我们可以从很多角度来看这个问题。

cues.en: So this is fairly well recovered. Again, it's a little bit anemic. The sorting grid hasn't reestablished itself, but it's doing a pretty good job considering it was a pretty major insult to the system. Alright, one last point.
cues.zh: 恢复得相当好。不过还是有点虚弱。排序网格还没重新建立起来，但考虑到系统受到了相当严重的损伤，它已经做得挺不错了。好，最后一点。

cues.en: I've made this grid so that it's about twice as wide plus some as it is high so that I mean if a datum, a really big datum starts at the upper right he's got to cross all the way down to the bottom before he can be sorted right and similarly the lower guys need to go up. So the amount of width affects how well we can sort and actually if we look
cues.zh: 我把这个网格做得宽度大约是高度的两倍多一点，意思是，如果一个数据、一个很大的数据从右上角开始，它得一路穿到底部才能被正确排序；同样，下面的数据也得往上走。所以宽度会影响排序效果，实际上如果我们看

cues.en: Here, this is a picture that's showing just the sorters, but instead of showing them as red, it shows them colored by what their threshold is. And we can see that near the input grid, there's lots of different colors, but as we move from right to left, the colors get more and more laminar, more and more uniform. And, you know, it looks like there isn't a whole lot happening in the last third of this grid. The colors seem fairly uniform.
cues.zh: 这里这张图只显示排序器，但不是把它们显示成红色，而是按阈值给它们着色。可以看到，靠近输入网格的地方有很多不同颜色，但从右往左移动，颜色变得越来越分层，越来越均匀。而且你看，这个网格最后三分之一看起来没多少事情在发生。颜色似乎相当均匀。

cues.en: But they're making increasingly fine distinctions between, you know, 805k and 830k, you know, whatever it is down at the bottom. So if we want, we can start stealing resources from this sorting thing.
cues.zh: 但它们在越来越精细地区分，比如 805k 和 830k，反正是底部那些数值。所以如果愿意，我们可以开始从这个排序系统里偷资源。

cues.en: And again, this is not a cooler thing. Instead of having the input and output grids nailed to the floor like this, we'd have some kind of movable bag that all this sorting would be happening in. But just for purposes of this demo, I've hacked this up. And if we start stealing space from this thing, the machine adjusts. Eventually, its sorting performance starts to degrade.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这并不是更酷的做法。与其像这样把输入和输出网格固定在地板上，我们会用一个可移动的袋子，所有排序都在里面发生。但只是为了这个演示，我临时拼凑了这个。如果我们开始从这里偷空间，机器会调整。最终，它的排序性能会开始下降。

cues.en: But now we've got all of this space over here. There are still events happening here. There's just nothing there doing anything. And if we want, we can put it back. All right. So that's it. A sorting machine that essentially can't not sort. It's got no real beginning. It's continually rebuilding itself at this basic level. Maybe we should turn it off. So that's it.
cues.zh: 但现在我们这边有了所有这些空间。这里仍然有事件在发生。只是那里没有任何东西在做事情。如果愿意，我们可以把它放回去。好吧。就是这样。一台本质上不可能不排序的排序机。它没有真正的起点。它在基本层面上不断重建自身。也许我们应该把它关掉。就是这样。

cues.en: This is obviously a different way to compute than the way that we've gotten used to it. But in a way, it's a lot more like how society computes. All of the stuff that we do in the world tolerates these little errors. The idea is that each computing element, instead of assuming that everything else is absolutely perfect, should assume that everything else is trying, but might not be.
cues.zh: 这显然是一种不同于我们习惯的计算方式。但某种程度上，它更像社会计算的方式。我们在世界上做的所有事情都容忍这些小误差。理念是，每个计算元件不应假设其他一切绝对完美，而应假设其他一切都在努力，但可能并不

cues.en: perfect. So computational elements that give a little better than they get, like the sorter doesn't try to get the correct answer, just tries to give a little better than it gets. Thanks for watching.
cues.zh: 完美。所以计算元件给出的比得到的稍好一点，就像排序器并不试图得到正确答案，只是试图给出比得到的稍好一点的结果。感谢观看。
